🔮 Gold / Central Bank De-Dollarization + Term Premium Repricing
 What the market is pricing in: Gold at $4,476 (+3.1% in 4W) continues its secular re-rating as central banks diversify reserves away from USD-denominated assets.
Peter Schiff's 8% Treasury yield warning is gaining traction.
Each failed Treasury auction or dollar weakness episode accelerates it.
Risk if wrong: Sharp Fed hike restores dollar credibility and term premium compresses.

Multiple forces are converging: rising Treasury yields (10Y at 4.78%, ↑2.7%) are being read not as a sign of economic strength but as a fiscal credibility crisis — the "bond vigilante" narrative that Peter Schiff amplified this weekend warning yields could reach 8%.
CNN's headline about "the war raising the price of money" and El-Erian's note about hyperscaler bond issuance crowding out Treasuries feed the same thesis.

The mechanical similarities are striking: yields were rising off historic lows, fiscal stimulus was flooding markets, gold had already had its run (up ~25% in 2020 before stalling), and retail began treating BTC as "gold but better" — a faster horse for the same debasement thesis.

Some macro funds view the move as structurally justified — rising yields without Fed intervention, geopolitical risk premium, and increasing institutional infrastructure (ETFs, custody) all provide legitimate demand floors that didn't exist in prior cycles.

When the narrative breaks: The trade dies if one of three things happens: (1) the Fed or Treasury takes dramatic action to cap long-end yields — a yield curve control signal or surprise buyback program — which would re-legitimize Treasuries as the safe haven and drain BTC's "broken bond market" thesis; (2) a sharp equity selloff pushes VIX above 30, triggering the historical pattern where BTC correlates back to risk assets and sells off alongside stocks as margin calls force liquidation; or (3) a regulatory shock — exchange enforcement action, tax rule change, or stablecoin crackdown — that disrupts the on-ramp infrastructure.
The narrative is reinforced by the Iran strikes, rising yields being read as fiscal unsustainability, and the Gold/Copper ratio at 670 (fear-elevated) confirming macro anxiety.
Peter Schiff's warning about 8% Treasury yields is exactly the type of content that gold bugs amplify.
